name: The Jayhawks
label: Twin/Tone
lede: A Minneapolis rockabilly guy and a guitarist who got hit by a car made a country-rock record from demos, and a phone call to their label got them a major deal.

eras.title: Two rockabilly guys and a car wreck
eras.text: Mark Olson and Gary Louris came up in rival Minneapolis rockabilly bands, then teamed up in a country-leaning band that sounded nothing like the punk and hardcore the Twin Cities were known for. A car accident nearly ended it before it had a proper record out.

years.h: [[Gary Louris|dd3e4c5c-b2fa-4614-9351-28362e31d015]] walks into [[Mark Olson|51655104-6963-4a60-a7db-c2c6de58f65d]]'s band
years.p: Louris, who played in Safety Last, joins Olson, bassist [[Marc Perlman|f0e45a77-5231-4cc6-8131-27b44ff3169b]] and drummer [[Norm Rogers|49f6514a-d4e8-4383-8099-56062daf16c4]], after seeing them play in Minneapolis.
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com dates Louris's arrival to February 1985. Wikipedia has the band starting a year earlier as a trio of Olson, bassist Caleb Palmiter and drummer Tommy Rey, before it went four-piece and Louris replaced guitarist Steve Retzler.

Louris told Magnet that he and Olson first met when each was in a rockabilly band on the local circuit: Louris in Safety Last, Olson in Stagger Lee.

years.h: Debut on Bunkhouse: a few thousand copies, Burrito comparisons
years.p: [[The Jayhawks|24ed5b09-02b1-47fe-bd83-6fa5270039b0]] press their first album for the tiny Bunkhouse label, and critics start reaching for the Flying Burrito Brothers.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Jayhawks · Wikipedia: Blue Earth
years.h: Louris survives a car accident, and the band nearly stalls
years.p: Encyclopedia.com describes near-fatal injuries; Wikipedia says Louris left the lineup for a stretch and returned to overdub guitar on the demos.
years.xp:
Dan Gaarder filled Louris's spot for a time, according to Wikipedia. The band was cutting demos in Minneapolis at the time, hoping to interest a bigger label.

Twin/Tone's Dave Ayers heard the tapes and suggested they be turned into an album.

eras.title: Demos on Twin/Tone, and one phone call
eras.text: Blue Earth started as demos and ended up a record. Nobody at Twin/Tone made a fuss, but somebody in Los Angeles happened to be on the line.

years.h: Blue Earth: demos become the Twin/Tone album
years.p: Recorded in Minneapolis with Jim Rondinelli and Tom Herbers, and finished after Louris returned to add guitar.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes the record was built from remixed demos cut between 1986 and 1989. Robert Christgau gave it an A-minus and called it "the obliquely songful followup the Burritos never made."

"Martin's Song" and "Two Angels" were re-recorded for Hollywood Town Hall three years later.

years.cap: Blue Earth, the record that got overheard.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jayhawks · The Current · Encyclopedia.com
years.h: A phone call to Twin/Tone gets the Jayhawks signed
years.p: Producer George Drakoulias, calling the office, hears Blue Earth playing in the background, asks what it is, and signs the band to Rick Rubin's Def American label.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and The Current place the deal in 1991. Encyclopedia.com and Wikipedia tell the story the same way: Drakoulias heard the record playing during a call to the label's A&R man, Dave Ayers.

The Jayhawks had no national profile at that point. The Current describes them working the Uptown Bar and the 400 Bar on the West Bank.

eras.title: Hollywood Town Hall
eras.text: Drakoulias made the record that put the Jayhawks in front of the rest of the country, then made a bigger, more expensive one. Olson walked away right after.

years.h: Hollywood Town Hall, cut at Hollywood Sound and Pachyderm
years.p: Drakoulias produces, with Nicky Hopkins and Benmont Tench on keys. Pitchfork's Stephen M. Deusner later calls it "the Jayhawks' greatest statement."
years.xp:
It peaked at No. 11 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 192 on the Billboard 200, Wikipedia reports. Singles were "Take Me with You (When You Go)," "Waiting for the Sun" and, in 1993, "Settled Down Like Rain."

Recording split between Hollywood Sound in Los Angeles and Pachyderm Studio in Minnesota.

years.h: [[Karen Grotberg|cdc80009-0f88-4cd9-b96b-944fe8d1c958]] joins on keys and harmony vocals
years.p: She comes aboard during the Hollywood Town Hall touring cycle and is a full member by the next record.

years.h: Golden Smog: a country-rock joke band with Twin Cities regulars
years.p: Louris and Perlman join Soul Asylum and Run Westy Run players for the covers EP On Golden Smog, credited under pseudonyms because of label contracts.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Golden Smog formally organized in 1989 as a country-rock reaction to the punk and hardcore that dominated the Twin Cities scene. The name comes from a Flintstones nickname for Fred Flintstone.

Its members have included Soul Asylum, Wilco and Jayhawks players; Kraig Johnson, later a Jayhawk, is a member today.

years.h: Eighteen months on the road, some of it behind the Black Crowes
years.p: The Jayhawks tour Hollywood Town Hall for a year and a half, Encyclopedia.com says, drawing new fans at rock crowds.
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com credits the touring with making the band, and dates Tim O'Reagan's arrival on drums to 1993 in place of Ken Callahan. Wikipedia dates O'Reagan's arrival to 1995.

Perlman told the magazine the band's stuff was "too quirky and not straightforward enough" for the mainstream.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tomorrow the Green Grass · Wikipedia: The Jayhawks
years.h: Tomorrow the Green Grass: Drakoulias again, a bigger budget
years.p: "Blue" reaches No. 33 in Canada; "Miss Williams' Guitar" is Olson's song for Victoria Williams, his then-girlfriend.
years.xp:
It peaked at No. 92 on the Billboard 200, Wikipedia reports. Don Heffington played drums on the album; Benmont Tench and violinist Lili Haydn guested.

Wikipedia says US sales disappointed given the cost of the production.

q: It wasn't a joyous ride, man.
years.h: Olson quits to move to Joshua Tree with Victoria Williams
years.p: He says he'd just married, found a house in Joshua Tree, and wanted to try something else. Louris tells Magnet Olson was tired of radio promotion.
years.xp:
Olson went on to make sparse, living-room records with Williams as the Original Harmony Ridge Creekdippers, taping some vocals in the bathroom, he told PopMatters. Paste quotes him saying he "just became a different person."

Tim O'Reagan was already the drummer and a second vocalist; Kraig Johnson came in on guitar.

eras.title: Louris takes the wheel
eras.text: With Olson in the desert, Louris wrote most of the songs and pushed toward psych, pop and power chords. Fans still argue over which Jayhawks they prefer.

years.h: Sound of Lies: Louris writes most of it, the country fades
years.p: Straight rock, psychedelia and acoustic songs, with Kraig Johnson on guitar for the first time.
years.xp: Louris told Magnet his inspirations were Brian Eno, the Clash, the Kinks and the Beatles more than country records. Little Village reports that the fanbase has divided since Sound of Lies over which era was better.

years.h: Smile: Bob Ezrin, drum loops, and a headline that stung
years.p: The New York Times reviewed it warmly under the title "What If You Made a Classic, and No One Cared?"
years.xp: Grotberg, pregnant, left before the tour and Jen Gunderman replaced her. "I'm Gonna Make You Love Me" ended up in Ralph Lauren commercials and on the Dawson's Creek Volume 2 soundtrack, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Louris drives out to Olson's house and they write a song
years.p: Olson told Elsewhere it was in 2001 that Louris came to his place and they wrote together for the first time in years.
years.xp: Louris told Magnet the thaw began with a request to write for the Dennis Quaid film The Rookie. He drove to Joshua Tree and they "talked through our old issues." Olson and Louris began touring together intermittently from 2001, per Paste.

years.h: Rainy Day Music: acoustic, back near country
years.p: Pedal steel and banjo from [[Stephen McCarthy|850adef3-13a0-4206-9126-44c5abbefaaf]] of the Long Ryders, and the band plays Austin City Limits for the first time.

years.h: Last show in Valencia, Spain, then a long silence
years.p: Wikipedia says the band stopped after touring Rainy Day Music, ending in Valencia.

eras.title: The hawks come back
eras.text: Olson and Louris toured as a duo, then the mid-90s lineup returned for festivals, a box of rarities and one new record. The reunion did not last.

years.h: Olson and Louris tour as a duo
years.p: Billed as "From the Jayhawks: An Evening with Mark Olson & Gary Louris, Together Again."
years.xp: Olson told PopMatters that they enjoyed writing songs that way and wanted people to hear how they sounded when first written. That became Ready for the Flood, released in January 2009 per Wikipedia (Olson dates the recording to 2008).

years.h: Primavera Sound, then the Basilica Block Party: the 1995 lineup returns
years.p: Louris, Olson, Perlman, Grotberg and O'Reagan play Barcelona on May 30 and Minneapolis on July 10.
years.xp:
Billboard reported the reunion in April 2009. Louris said the plan was to play festivals, and hoped for Bonnaroo the year after.

Paste dates a one-off at Spain's Azkena Rock Festival to September 2009; Wikipedia's timeline says 2008 in one place and 2009 in another.

years.h: Music from the North Country, a Louris-supervised anthology
years.p: Sony Legacy releases highlights, B-sides, rarities and videos.
years.xp: Paste says compiling the anthology helped inspire the full lineup's return.

years.h: Webster Hall: Hollywood Town Hall one night, Tomorrow the Green Grass the next
years.p: The reunited five play each album front to back on January 20 and 21, part of a Toronto-to-Minneapolis run.
years.xp: Legacy had just reissued both albums as collector's editions, with the Mystery Demos disc of 1992 recordings by Olson and Louris. The mini-tour also hit Philadelphia, Chicago and Minneapolis.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mockingbird Time · Wikipedia: The Jayhawks
years.h: Mockingbird Time: the first Olson album since 1995
years.p: Recorded Nov 5 to Dec 4, 2010 at the Terrarium in Minneapolis, produced by Louris; it enters the Billboard 200 at No. 38.
years.xp: They wrote in Louris's apartment, at Olson's Joshua Tree home and in a cabin in northern Minnesota, and cut 18 songs, 16 of them new. AllMusic's Mark Deming called it the strongest since Hollywood Town Hall.

years.h: Olson leaves again after the Mockingbird Time tour
years.p: Wikipedia's Mockingbird Time page says Olson complained about money and songwriting credits, and Louris called it "a fiasco" that left a bad taste.
years.xp: Little Village reports Olson cited personal differences and band business, and that Louris was being treated for painkiller addiction at the time. Louris told Rolling Stone Country it took getting clean and sober to appreciate what he had, including the Jayhawks.

eras.title: Four voices, no frontman
eras.text: Without Olson, Louris turned the band into a group of songwriters and singers, working with R.E.M.'s Peter Buck and the Kinks' Ray Davies.

years.h: Reissues of Sound of Lies, Smile and Rainy Day Music bring the band back
years.p: The 1997 lineup tours for the deluxe editions, playing songs it hadn't touched in a decade.
years.xp: The two-LP editions were remastered by Vic Anesini; Smile got its first U.S. vinyl release.

years.src: Wikipedia: Paging Mr. Proust · Little Village
years.h: Paging Mr. Proust: Peter Buck and Tucker Martine in Portland
years.p: Three songs are full-band co-writes; Louris said he wanted to feature three good vocalists.
years.xp: It peaked at No. 75 on the Billboard 200. Kraig Johnson left before release and John Jackson, who played on it, joined the touring band.

years.h: NPR Tiny Desk Concert
years.p: The band plays a stripped-down set at the NPR offices.
years.xp: The performance is listed on NPR Music's Tiny Desk page dated August 5, 2016.

yt: Ray Davies & the Jayhawks, "Wings of Fantasy"
years.h: Ray Davies makes Americana with the Jayhawks behind him
years.p: The former Kinks singer records his U.S. memoir album with the band, then a follow-up, Our Country: Americana Act II, in 2018.

years.h: Original drummer Norm Rogers dies of cancer
years.p: Wikipedia lists him as the band's drummer from 1984 to 1988.

years.h: Back Roads and Abandoned Motels: a fifth member, John Jackson
years.p: Released on Sony Legacy with John Jackson as fifth member and co-producer.

years.h: XOXO: every core member writes and sings
years.p: Louris, Perlman, O'Reagan and Grotberg each take lead vocals on songs; the band plays CBS This Morning: Saturday on June 27.

years.h: A star on the First Avenue wall
years.p: The band earns a star on the Minneapolis club's outside mural. Journalist Steve Marsh called it possibly the city's most prestigious public honor for an artist.
years.xp: Stars go to acts with sold-out shows or significant cultural contribution to the club.
